featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience at Vedant Central Hospital, Ghatkopar West. My wife went there for her hernia operation because they said Ayushman Card was accepted.

Initially, the staff informed us that the operation would be covered under the Aayushman scheme and we only needed to pay for tests, medicines, and other small expenses.

After completing all the tests, the staff suddenly changed their statement and said the operation could not be done under the Ayushman scheme and demanded around ₹80,000 for surgery, bed charges, and medicines are separately Charges.

Why mislead patients in the beginning if the treatment is not actually covered? Patients waste time, money, and go through mental stress. Very unprofessional and disappointing management experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.

Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

It was early morning and my sister had sudden pain in her stomach. Looking at the pain I was quite evident that it was due to stone. As we were near to Parakh hospital we reached there. As per doctor's advice ultrasound was done and as I thought it was due to stone only. We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Exceptional Care & Trustworthy Expertise—A Deeply Appreciated Recovery Experience of Rohit Vinerkar

My recent admission to Zynova Shalby Hospital for Typhoid Fever (Nov 13-17) reaffirmed the trust my family and I place in this institution, particularly after my mother’s successful knee replacement in 2022.

I approached Dr. Satvik Patel for a second opinion on November 12th. I was thoroughly impressed with his approach; he carefully assessed my situation and ordered the necessary tests. The following day, with the diagnosis confirmed, Dr. Patel advised an SOS admission.

Dr. Patel's Professional Excellence and New Discoveries -
During my treatment for typhoid, another concern related to my health came forward. Dr. Patel immediately took charge, providing guidance and treatment in a cool and composed manner. He is truly the MS Dhoni of medicine, maintaining his calm demeanor and delivering effective treatment under pressure. This ability to manage complex situations without stress was immensely reassuring.
Furthermore, his thoroughness brought to light a fascinating personal detail: I apparently have an abundance of RBCs in my blood. Dr. Patel, not only provided treatment for the fever but also gave me some great life advice—I've been kindly recommended to donate blood often. (It seems I now generate content both for the screen and for the blood bank. Who knew my body was producing a surplus!)
His ability to explain all these complex findings clearly in excellent Marathi instantly built a strong and enduring connection. It was incredibly reassuring to hear detailed medical advice given with such clarity and ease. "तुमचा स्वभाव आणि समजावण्याची पद्धत, सर, अगदी कौतुकास्पद आहे."
We are now hoping to resolve this new challenge soon under his expert care.

Staff, Facilities, and Comfort -
The medical attention and human touch provided by the staff were consistently excellent. The nurses were attentive and meticulous in my care.
Even while recovering in Room 605 (a choice made for the Vastu and morning sunlight), I felt well-supported and comfortable. The colour choice of the interior is lively, and the view from the window is amazing, contributing greatly to the positive atmosphere. I even watched the India vs. South Africa cricket test!

On November 14th, the staff's care gave me enough comfort to watch the broadcast of Doraemon Movie Earth Symphony on Disney India. As I was the Assistant Dubbing Director and Mixing Engineer for that project, it was a unique and meaningful experience to connect with my work while recovering. The quality and timing of the food service were also good.

A Critical Point for Management Consideration -
While the patient care is truly awesome, I must address a severe pain point that impacts accessibility for many patients: The security deposit requested during the admission process is significantly higher than usual.
It is challenging for patients, especially those with high-premium insurance coverage, to submit such a substantial deposit. If Zynova Shalby’s core mission is to serve humanity, I strongly urge the management to reassess this security deposit policy. Streamlining this financial aspect would remove a severe point of friction and ensure that exceptional medical care is accessible to all.

Overall: I am grateful for the expert medical treatment and compassionate attention I received. Thank you, Zynova, and especially Dr. Patel, for taking excellent care of me. "हम दिल से आपके आभारी हैं। एक मरीज को और क्या चाहिए? सब कुछ बहुत अच्छा था।" I am focusing on a swift recovery and look forward to being fit soon!

Extremely disappointing experience.

Our 81-year-old grandmother has been admitted in the ICU for several days, and while we understand that critical care treatment is expensive, the lack of transparency and communication has been deeply frustrating.

The bill has already crossed several lakhs, yet our family has struggled to get clear explanations regarding her condition, prognosis, and treatment progress. Every day we were told to wait for a few more days, but there was little clarity on whether there was any measurable improvement.

What was even more stressful was the constant pressure on family members to arrange medicines and consumables, sometimes late at night, while we were already dealing with an emotionally devastating situation. Families with critically ill loved ones deserve compassion, transparency, timely access to reports, and honest communication. Unfortunately, that has not been our experience.

I hope the hospital reviews its patient-family communication process and treats families with more empathy during such difficult times.

Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.
